findings.F1: Over its 8,559 long bars the book earned a gross sum of 15.82 for 1.55 in fees, while its 8,762 short bars lost a gross 4.21 and still paid 1.52 in fees, so the short half is a net loss of about 5.7 against the long half's net 14.3.
findings.F2: Shorts lose in absolute terms because the coins drift up: on short bars the coin's next-day return averaged -0.000134 against +0.002529 on long bars, and in the negative-forecast non-overlapping 7-day samples the raw forward return was near zero (+0.0034 with no 30-day history, +0.0013 when the 30-day return was positive, only -0.0033 when it was negative, 1,253 cases), even though their return net of the coin's mean was -0.0095 (t -2.69).
findings.F3: The long side's gain sits where the coin is already rising: long bars with a positive 30-day return earned a mean 0.002295 a bar (sum 10.99 of the 15.82), against 0.000802 with a negative 30-day return; positive-forecast samples returned 0.027 over 7 days when the 30-day return was positive (excess 0.018, 629 cases) and only 0.0107 when it was negative (excess 0.0014, 223 cases).
findings.F4: The forecast's top fifth (mean +17.2) was followed by a 7-day return of 0.0277 and the bottom fifth (mean -14.6) by +0.0043, so even the strongest negative forecasts came before a rise and gave no edge to a short.
findings.F5: Dropping the shorts in a rough rebuild of the daily book (daily mean over coins of gain minus fee) lifts the mean daily return from 0.00049 to 0.00082, the Sharpe from 0.48 to 1.08, the deepest fall from -52% to -31% and the Calmar from 0.22 to 0.96.
findings.F6: The book's deepest fall, -52%, ran 1,001 days from w2 to w10 while holding the coins lost 23% over the same span, so the book fell further than the market. Its daily returns had a correlation of -0.016 with holding's, its mean daily return was 0.000498 against holding's 0.00118, and its Sharpe was 0.49 against 0.55. Together with F1 and F2, this points to a book that kept shorting through the coins' rebounds.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 14-day return, the higher its return over the next 7 days, and the more so the higher its 30-day return, with the largest rises following strong two-week gains inside a rising month.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long the coins with the strongest two-week rise and lean harder when the month is also up, rather than shorting the coins that fell, whose next week still drifts up.
ideas.name: two-week momentum in rising months

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 14-day return while its 30-day return is positive, the larger its 7-day return over the next 7 days, measured above the coin's usual 7-day return.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size up longs on coins whose two-week and one-month moves are both up, and size them down where the month is falling, since momentum there adds almost nothing above the coin's drift.
ideas.name: trend-aligned momentum strength
